subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient keep unlimited reconnects by default and expose an opt-in maxReconnectAttempts policy, or should core impose a default reconnect ceiling?
rationale: Current main has no cap, but issue discussion, node-host source, and the linked PR all show long-lived node-host recovery may rely on indefinite reconnects, so the permanent retry contract is a compatibility/product decision rather than a purely mechanical fix.

options.title: Default unlimited, opt-in cap
options.body: Keep existing node-host behavior and let short-lived clients opt into bounded reconnects through a narrow GatewayClient option.

options.title: Default bounded reconnects
options.body: Add a global default retry cap and require long-lived callers to explicitly opt out, accepting upgrade risk for existing deployments.

options.title: No reconnect cap
options.body: Treat indefinite reconnect as intended and close the linked PR after confirming listener/process leaks are solved elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Default unlimited, opt-in cap
recommendation.body: Keep existing node-host behavior and let short-lived clients opt into bounded reconnects through a narrow GatewayClient option.

likelyOwner.reason: The original GatewayClient control-plane behavior and most historical ownership on this path trace to steipete, and this decision is about the core gateway retry contract.
